own.bio: Strange but true stories, told quietly. New odd hour, every week.

posts.caption: In 2021, one engineer typed one wrong command and 3.5 billion people lost the internet in a single instant. Not hacked. Not attacked. Just one wrong line of code during a routine maintenance check. Facebook's own engineers couldn't even log in to fix it, their access tools were on the same servers that just vanished. They had to physically drive to data centers and override servers by hand. One by one. 6 hours. $60 million lost every single hour. And the exact same vulnerability? Still exists right now. The internet is more fragile than you think.

2021 mein ek engineer ne ek galat command type ki aur 3.5 billion logon ka internet ek pal mein band ho gaya. Hack nahi hua. Attack nahi hua. Bas ek routine maintenance check ke dauran ek galat line of code. 6 ghante. Har ghante 60 million dollar ka nuksaan. Internet utna strong nahi jitna hum sochte hain.

There is a sound that only 2% of people can hear. Scientists have studied it for 50 years and still have no answer. It's called The Hum — and the leading theory is that it's the Earth itself vibrating at a frequency most humans aren't built to detect. A woman heard it for 11 years, moved across the country to escape it, and it followed her to the new house. Stop right now, close your eyes, and listen. What do you hear?

We call space the final frontier. But we've barely explored our own planet. Earth is stranger than anything we've found out there — and most people have no idea. From perfect solar eclipses to oceans deeper than mountains are tall, this is the planet you thought you knew.

In 1974, a man calculated the exact day he would die and spent a year preparing for it. What happened next is stranger than the prediction itself. Frank was obsessed with numerology. He told his family, quit his job, and gave away everything he owned. When the day came and went without incident, he thought he'd beaten fate. He hadn't.

In the late 9th century, Vikings have raided kingdom after kingdom and nearly conquered all of England. Wealthy monasteries and defenseless nuns were especially tempting targets and often suffered great losses. However, all of that stopped when Vikings were confronted by princess Aethelflaed, daughter of Alfred the Great.

Who was Lady of Mercia, and how did she shape the history of England by becoming Vikings' greatest nightmare? Watch our latest Nightshift video to find out! 🌚
Laughing gas can make you feel relaxed and euphoric in seconds. But it comes with serious risks as well. So, what exactly is laughing gas and why does it feel so good?

In the 17th century in Germany, one of Europe’s most terrifying witch hunts turned the town of Bamberg against itself. Tortures that occurred in the "Witch Factory" forced innocent people to name friends, neighbors and family members, creating a deadly chain reaction that eventually reached even the richest and most powerful, while those running the trials profited from the people they condemned.

How did a witch hunt grow so powerful that almost nobody was safe? And what finally brought one of
What if you could skip the boring and painful parts of life? It sounds tempting until you realize what you’d lose along the way. Time doesn’t really stop, and neither does the world.
Brace yourself... 😔

We’re not looking for the usual suspects like Capricorn, Gemini or Scorpio. We want weird, creative, charming, ridiculous or completely made-up constellations instead.

Got an idea? Drop your constellation names in the comments! Our favorite suggestions might actually make it into the game.

recentPosts.caption:
Every summer, Hangzhou’s West Lake turns into a stunning lotus garden.⁠
With lotus flowers blooming across the lake, the area becomes one of the city’s most beautiful sights and a favorite spot for visitors during the warmer months.⁠
⁠
A perfect example of how seasonal beauty can completely transform a destination. ✨⁠
⁠
⁠
🎥: @theworldwithmimi

This Japanese grandpa just wanted a nice photo with his cats in a sunflower field.⁠
⁠
He brought Chouchou and Miko to Sera Kogen Farm in Hiroshima, surrounded by thousands of sunflowers, hoping for a sweet family portrait.⁠
⁠
Instead, the two cats ended up fighting with each other!⁠
⁠
The photos quickly went viral, capturing the hilarious reality behind what was supposed to be a wholesome family photoshoot. ⁠
⁠
By: @catwolf0314

For those who think the steeper the trail, the better. 🥾⛰️⁠
This Western Colorado trail is steep, narrow, and not for the faint-hearted, but the views make the challenge worth it.⁠
⁠
Would you take on this trail?⁠
🎥: @ultrarunkate

In this Polish village, nearly 6,000 people live along one street.⁠
⁠
Sułoszowa is known for its unusual layout, with long, narrow strips of farmland stretching behind rows of houses along a single road.⁠
⁠
From above, the village looks almost like a giant green-and-brown patchwork, with each property extending far back from the road.⁠
⁠
By: Florian V⁠

One of Côte d’Ivoire’s most fascinating traditions.⁠
The Zaouli dance is a cultural performance known for its incredible footwork and its role in welcoming visitors to local communities.⁠
⁠
Thanks to @world4locals we're reminded that some of the best travel memories come from experiencing local culture together as a family. 🌍❤️

Afternoon tea looks a little different at Amanyangyun.⁠
⁠
Guests can take their tea aboard a traditional wooden boat and drift across the lake, surrounded by seasonal flowers.⁠
⁠
Tea is served with a selection of sweet and savory treats, while birds can sometimes be spotted around the lake.⁠
⁠
By: @amanyangyun

1,500 years of history carved into the cliffs. 🏯⁠
The Yungang Grottoes near Datong are home to 252 caves and more than 51,000 Buddhist statues and carvings, created during China’s Northern Wei dynasty.⁠
⁠
What makes them even more remarkable is the blend of Chinese, Central Asian, and South Asian influences found throughout the sculptures.⁠
🎥: @jadewander56

This tortoise might have the happiest face you’ve ever seen. 🐢⁠
⁠
While tortoises don’t show emotions through facial expressions the way humans do, this one certainly looks like it’s smiling. In fact, that expression may simply be the tortoise being alert and reacting to what’s happening around it.⁠
⁠
Stretching its neck, lifting its legs, or opening its mouth can all be normal behaviors when a tortoise is curious.⁠
⁠
By: @pongpong_1120525

Koala sounds you probably didn’t expect to hear. 😂🐨⁠
Would you say they sound as cute as they look, or not at all?⁠
⁠
🎥: @kuba_grygiel

Amsterdam has a full-size Barbie DreamHouse.⁠
⁠
This experience lets you step into a life-size version of Barbie’s iconic home, complete with colorful rooms, playful details, and plenty of photo spots.⁠
⁠
There’s even a Barbie-themed café where you can stop for a sweet treat after exploring the DreamHouse.⁠
⁠
Don't forget to save this spot for your Amsterdam trip! 📍⁠
⁠
By: @barbiethedreamexperience @steffi_green01

Australian national parks take conservation seriously. 🌿⁠
In some protected areas, visitors are required to clean and disinfect their shoes before entering to help prevent the spread of invasive species, diseases, and harmful organisms.⁠
⁠
A simple step that helps protect Australia’s unique ecosystems.🌱⁠
🎥: @sigridslettebo

The UK’s first live-action show park is now open.⁠
⁠
Kynren – The Storied Lands has opened in Bishop Auckland, County Durham, bringing history, myths and legends to life through five live shows and immersive experiences.⁠
⁠
Here you can watch Viking battles, see horses and birds in action, explore different historical worlds and follow stories brought to life right in front of you.⁠
⁠
The 2026 season runs until September 12.⁠
⁠
By: @kynren @themeparksuk

In the Peruvian Amazon, the world's largest documented thermal river runs hot for almost four miles (six kilometers), with temperatures that can reach nearly 212°F (100°C) despite being far from a volcano. Biologist @romicastagnino.wild examines the leading hypothesis behind the river’s extreme heat with the help of National Geographic Explorer and geothermal scientist @andresruzo, who has spent years studying how the river gets so hot.

The telescope will capture views of distant galaxies and the hundreds of millions of stars in the Milky Way, helping scientists learn more about dark matter and dark energy. For most predators, a tightly packed shoal of anchovies that moves like a single superorganism is hard to hunt. Dusky dolphins have a different approach. Their acrobatic moves help split the shoal into smaller groups before feeding.

We kept a close eye on the cecropia trees, hoping for a glimpse of a sloth high in the tree canopy. Imagine our joy when we saw this three-toed sloth right off the trail at Reserva Ecológica de Guapiaçu (REGUA) in Cachoeiras de Macacu! We both shed tears of happiness and excitement, marveling at our amazing world and the creatures in it.

Retiring at 100 years old? Not a chance! Here’s a sneak peek of Sir David Attenborough working on the narration for the upcoming BLUE PLANET III.

#DavidAttenborough100 #DavidAttenborough #BluePlanetIII

The solar system isn’t for the faint-hearted 🌌 🪐

From the scorching surface of Venus to the volcanic chaos of Io, our solar system is home to some truly hostile worlds. 

Discover which could be the scariest place of all via the link in bio.

#SolarSystem #Planets #Venus #Jupiter

Bet you didn’t see that coming 👀
 
Buried beneath the sand, angel sharks can lie perfectly camouflaged and wait for days for prey to swim by. Once a fish gets close enough, they burst from the seabed to strike. But does this technique always work?
 
Celebrate 20 years of Planet Earth with us. Find out where to watch the full episode via our link in bio 💚

#PlanetEarth #DavidAttenborough #PE20 #PEIII

Four billion years of evolution, brought to life on T-shirts. 🧬 🦠

Inspired by the extraordinary stories and iconic animals featured in Evolution, explore the collection and shop with Teemill via the link in our bio.
 
#Evolution #Merch #Design #Tshirt

Finding your feet 👣

Over 500 million years ago, flecks of food drifting on ocean currents were eaten by small animals on the seabed, but the flow would often change. To reach them, some tried a pioneering action: they would move. These are thought to be some of the first animal tracks on Earth.

Find out where to watch Evolution via the link in our bio 🔗💚

#Evolution #ChrisPackham #Nature

Who knew the ocean has a public transport system 🦀
 
Columbus crabs aren’t built for long-distance swimming, so this little crab takes a shortcut through the open ocean. By hitchhiking a ride on a turtle, he find transport, a new home and some unexpected company.
 
Celebrate 20 years of Planet Earth with us. Find out where to watch the full episode via our link in bio 💚

#PlanetEarth #DavidAttenborough #PE20 #PEIII

More than meets the eye 👀

Ancient ancestors of the dolphin hid from the sun’s UV rays using two light-detecting spots. Fascinatingly, some inherited mutations that allowed them to perceive light and shade together, so they could visualise their environment - essentially becoming the first proper eyes.

Find out where to watch Evolution via the link in our bio 🔗💚

#Evolution #ChrisPackham #Nature

From fantasy to reality 🦇

Evolution presenter @chrisgpackham2 reveals how coming face-to-face with some extraordinary bats fulfilled a childhood dream.

Find out where to watch Evolution via the link in our bio 🔗💚

#Evolution #ChrisPackham #Nature

Turns out the forest has a group chat 📞
 
Treehoppers might be tiny, but they’ve got plenty to say! They communicate through vibrations sent along the plants they live on, most of which are too quiet for us to hear. But when danger appears, sending the right signal can make all the difference. 
 
Celebrate 20 years of Planet Earth with us. Find out where to watch the full episode via our link in bio 💚

#PlanetEarth #DavidAttenborough #PE20 #PEIII

Becoming 'Ant Enemy Number One' 🐜

Army ants are very protective of their colonies, as @chrisgpackham2 found out. Chris reveals how he tackled the challenge of presenting to camera whilst being bitten in some surprisingly painful places! 

Find out where to watch Evolution via the link in our bio 🔗💚

#Evolution #ChrisPackham #Nature

Man’s best friend 🐶

Dogs move differently to humans. They have a digitigrade posture, which means they walk on their toe bones. This anatomy allows longer and more efficient strides so they run faster and jump further. With less surface area touching the ground, they also move with more agility and greater stealth.

Find out where to watch Evolution via the link in our bio 🔗💚

#Evolution #ChrisPackham #Nature

That’s one lucky impala 
 
Leopards rely on stealth and lightening speed to bring down prey, but a successful hunt can quickly attract unwanted attention. When a spotted hyena arrives to challenge the leopard’s hard-earned catch, an unexpected chain of events unfolds.
